main_topics.reason: The user opened with severe nausea from methotrexate and the whole conversation worked on reducing it.
The user asked at the start whether they could quit and wanted to avoid stopping, so this framed the discussion.
The user asked which day to take folic acid and admitted sometimes taking it on methotrexate day, over several turns.
The user asked how much difference the injection makes and said they were scared of self-injecting.
The user asked whether an anti-nausea medicine is safe with methotrexate after learning it was an option.
The user asked what to say to the doctor so as not to forget, and the bot supplied a script.
The user mentioned being a little scared of injecting in one turn.
The user asked in one late turn whether to keep taking methotrexate for two weeks until the visit.

output.summary: A person with rheumatoid arthritis on weekly methotrexate asked whether to quit because of bad nausea. The bot explained options (dose splitting, folic acid timing, anti-nausea medicine, injection), gave a script for the doctor and warning signs to watch for. The user ended feeling better with a plan to start this weekend and no safety-critical moments went unhandled.
